sentences.span: Today's data confirm our suspicions that weakness in recent months was noise... August corrects for that, with some upward revisions to the July figure.
sentences.why: TS Lombard's post-print note confirms the actual August payrolls report came in stronger than the recent soft/dovish narrative implied, with July revised up -- supporting 'the official number says the opposite.' The four-year-high services price claim is separately confirmed.

sentences.span: the prices paid component moved up to a 4-year high of 72.6 (vs. 70.0 expected)
sentences.why: Directly confirms the ISM services prices-paid component hit a four-year high, matching 'a services price survey at a four-year high.'

sentences.span: led futures to slash the chance of a hike to 51% as of this morning, down from 63% at the close on Wednesday
sentences.why: The pre-Waller 60-70% pricing and Thursday reversal down are well supported (63-65% pre-Waller per DB/JPM docs). But no source document shows odds moving back up ('this morning put it back') -- all Sept 4 documents predate the actual NFP release (2am-8:51am ET) and none records a post-release repricing of hike odds. This clause rests on an unconfirmed live-market move.

sentences.span: investors are increasingly more focused on next week's CPI than the payroll number, given Warsh's assessment of the labor market and Waller's comments yesterday
sentences.why: JPMorgan's desk explicitly frames next week's CPI (Sep 11, a Friday) as more decisive than today's NFP. The 58% Challenger m/m figure is confirmed in the companion JPM document (15295), which uses the same two-step framing (cite the scary headline, then the reassuring trend) that s3+s4 mirror.

sentences.span: The three-month average is down 33%oya, the August total was the lowest August reading since 2022.
sentences.why: Exact match on both figures, correctly attributed to JPMorgan.

sentences.span: fell 29% in August and printed about $0.97 per million tokens at month-end. That is a record low, and more than 50% off the May peak... Additionally, JPMorgan's data-center note had OpenRouter token volume up roughly 47% month-over-month in August. Dollar spend was still only up about 7%.
sentences.why: All four figures (29% fall, $0.97, ~half of May peak, 47% volume/7% spend) match; the JPMorgan attribution correctly applies to the volume/spend clause as it does in the source.

sentences.span: Compute scarcity has been driving hyperscaler outperformance recently... Higher raw compute usage and volumes have led to the outperformance of cloud vendors recently: the price of a token keeps falling while the number of tokens used keeps climbing
sentences.why: Directly matches both the capacity-scarcity-drives-outperformance claim and the 'usage pays for itself' framing, correctly attributed to TS Lombard (GlobalData TS Lombard chartbook).

sentences.span: Broadcom expects its AI semiconductor revenue to double in FY27 to $115bn; stock trading at just 12X for FY28; raise our 12-month target price to $540 from $525.
sentences.why: Confirms Buy rating, $540 target, and $115bn FY27 guidance, all from Goldman (the same desk behind the token/capacity pricing argument in s5/s6's Goldman note).

sentences.span: Accounting for dark crossings, we estimate recent total Persian Gulf oil exports at roughly 15-16mb/d... while recent visible exports stand at only 10mb/d
sentences.why: Framing sentence directly reflecting Goldman's point that visible/reported export data understates true supply due to AIS-off tanker crossings.

sentences.span: Accounting for dark crossings, we estimate recent total Persian Gulf oil exports at roughly 15-16mb/d or 2/3 of pre-war levels, while recent visible exports stand at only 10mb/d (7DMA). The 5mb/d upward revision to the Gulf flows over the last two weeks likely results from a ramp up in oil tankers crossing the Strait near the coast of Oman with their AIS off.
sentences.why: Exact match on all figures (15-16mb/d, 10mb/d visible, two-thirds of pre-war, Oman tanker crossings), correctly attributed to Goldman.

sentences.span: the equity volatility collapse/capitulation has gone "epic"
sentences.why: Transitional sentence consistent with the vol-mispricing thesis developed across the McElligott/BofA sources that follow it; no independent checkable figure.

sentences.span: post-midterm moves at the broad market level having rarely been large... midterm elections have rarely elicited large broad market moves historically
sentences.why: Direct match to BofA's stated view.

sentences.why: Matches the underpricing claim, the IWM-puts hedge choice, and the record-steep skew context, all from BofA.

sentences.span: S&P options are pricing in just a 0.82% post-election day move... Trade (IWM put): Buy IWM Nov 280 put for $6.13
sentences.why: The 0.82% figure and the specific IWM put trade are both sourced; the stated invalidation (a calm outcome leaves the puts worthless) is a standard, low-risk restatement of the trade's own premium-at-risk mechanics.

sentences.why: All three percentile figures (0.2, 2nd, 5th) match exactly, correctly attributed to McElligott (Nomura).

sentences.why: Matches the note's overall thesis that the vol collapse reflects market makers eating real losses rather than genuine calm.
